Close still life in a dark timber grain room, low angle at sack height. A stack of fat hemp sacks bulging with millet. One arrow with red #e8563f fletching is driven deep into the topmost sack, buried almost to the feathers, the shaft still quivering; the hemp has split around it and millet pours out of the wound in a heavy golden stream, piling and bouncing on the packed-earth floor. A single oil lamp on a sack beside it is the hard warm key, dusty-gold #e8a04a light raking across the grain stream and the strained weave of the sacks. Dust motes and flying grains as glowing bokeh, crushed umber dark beyond. Hot, sudden, suggestive. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
